purpose: Record which installed AI helper CLIs were detected locally and how they can safely assist SEIS AI without receiving secrets, repository dumps, credentials, live SSH access, deployment authority, or permission expansion.

helpers.role: primary implementation and repository editing agent
helpers.safeUse: implementation, validation, commit preparation, and final integration under SEIS governance

helpers.role: architecture and safety reviewer when authenticated
helpers.safeUse: review-only after authentication and with no secrets or private keys in prompt context

helpers.role: broad-context documentation and Google ecosystem reviewer when authenticated
helpers.safeUse: plan-mode review after authentication and with explicit no-secret prompt boundaries

helpers.role: secondary reasoning and contradiction review when authenticated
helpers.safeUse: plan-mode review after authentication and without workspace dumps or credentials
explicitly scoped review or run mode only after permission boundaries are chosen

helpers.role: local model experimentation and private draft review
helpers.safeUse: local-only draft review; output must be filtered for hidden reasoning and never treated as authoritative

acceptedCollaborationEvidence: Codex is the active implementation agent for this local repository turn.
Installed helper availability was verified by command presence and version checks.
Claude, Gemini, and Qwen review attempts were blocked by missing authentication and were not treated as successful assistance.
Ollama local model availability was verified, but the review attempt was aborted because output was not concise and was not accepted as guidance.
nonClaimBoundaries: No external AI helper was given secrets, private keys, tokens, .env contents, host credentials, deployment authority, or broad repository dumps.
No blocked or aborted helper output is treated as validation success.
No helper may install plugins, expand permissions, run live SSH, deploy, push, merge, or train models without explicit human approval.
Installed AI collaboration is advisory and remains subordinate to SEIS governance, local validators, tests, and human review.
